tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Recall that if the random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed over the interval $[a,b],$ then $X$ has the following probability density function:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14211554/assets/af2afd72c74a9d7ca810886490baf28610cb743cbe8c8595158cfc2af702b7fa.svg)

It can be shown that the expected value and variance of $X$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =\frac{a+b}{2} \\ \text{Var}[X] & =\frac{(b-a)^{2}}{12}\end{aligned}
$$

The result for $\textrm{E}[X]$ is intuitive as it's simply the midpoint of the interval $[a,b].$ 

We will derive both of these results at the end of the lesson.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14211554/assets/af2afd72c74a9d7ca810886490baf28610cb743cbe8c8595158cfc2af702b7fa.svg)

$$

tutorials.name: Deriving the Formula for the Mean
tutorials.problem:
If $X\sim U[a,b],$ then $X$ has the following probability density function:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14211554/assets/be9457e598579e35be37d8fcc86663f4229e6193f02b11c49242d63858406a3b.svg)

We can compute the formula for $\textrm E[X]$ using the usual definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{a}^{b}xf(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{a}^{b}\frac{x}{b-a}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{b-a}\cdot {\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}|}_{a}^{b} \\  & =\frac{1}{2(b-a)}\cdot ({b}^{2}-{a}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2(b-a)}\cdot (b-a)(b+a) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\cancel{(b-a)}}\cdot \cancel{(b-a)}(b+a) \\  & =\frac{a+b}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
tutorials.title: Deriving the Formula for the Mean
tutorials.content:
If $X\sim U[a,b],$ then $X$ has the following probability density function:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14211554/assets/be9457e598579e35be37d8fcc86663f4229e6193f02b11c49242d63858406a3b.svg)

We can compute the formula for $\textrm E[X]$ using the usual definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{a}^{b}xf(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{a}^{b}\frac{x}{b-a}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{b-a}\cdot {\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}|}_{a}^{b} \\  & =\frac{1}{2(b-a)}\cdot ({b}^{2}-{a}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2(b-a)}\cdot (b-a)(b+a) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\cancel{(b-a)}}\cdot \cancel{(b-a)}(b+a) \\  & =\frac{a+b}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Deriving the Formula for the Variance
tutorials.problem:
If $X\sim U[a,b],$ then $X$ has the following probability density function:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14211554/assets/579372cf7b7880117ff6e7b4e1f063b29e42f886b06e2277e2dcb1f1240ff11d.svg)

To compute $\textrm{Var}[X],$ we use the relation

$$
\textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm{E}[X^2] - (\textrm{E}[X])^2.
$$

First, we compute $\textrm E[X^2]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{a}^{b}{x}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{a}^{b}\frac{{x}^{2}}{b-a}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{b-a}\cdot {\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}|}_{a}^{b} \\  & =\frac{1}{3(b-a)}\cdot ({b}^{3}-{a}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3(b-a)}\cdot (b-a)({b}^{2}+ab+{a}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\cancel{(b-a)}}\cdot \cancel{(b-a)}({b}^{2}+ab+{a}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}({b}^{2}+ab+{a}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\textrm E[X] = \dfrac12(b+a),$ we have

$$
(\textrm E[X])^2 = \dfrac14(b^2+2ab+a^2).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-(\text{E}[X])^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}({b}^{2}+ab+{a}^{2})-\frac{1}{4}({b}^{2}+2ab+{a}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{4}{12}({b}^{2}+ab+{a}^{2})-\frac{3}{12}({b}^{2}+2ab+{a}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(4{b}^{2}+4ab+4{a}^{2})-\frac{1}{12}(3{b}^{2}+6ab+3{a}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{12}({b}^{2}-2ab+{a}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(b-a)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
tutorials.title: Deriving the Formula for the Variance
tutorials.content:
If $X\sim U[a,b],$ then $X$ has the following probability density function:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14211554/assets/579372cf7b7880117ff6e7b4e1f063b29e42f886b06e2277e2dcb1f1240ff11d.svg)

To compute $\textrm{Var}[X],$ we use the relation

$$
\textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm{E}[X^2] - (\textrm{E}[X])^2.
$$

First, we compute $\textrm E[X^2]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{a}^{b}{x}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{a}^{b}\frac{{x}^{2}}{b-a}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{b-a}\cdot {\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}|}_{a}^{b} \\  & =\frac{1}{3(b-a)}\cdot ({b}^{3}-{a}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3(b-a)}\cdot (b-a)({b}^{2}+ab+{a}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\cancel{(b-a)}}\cdot \cancel{(b-a)}({b}^{2}+ab+{a}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}({b}^{2}+ab+{a}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\textrm E[X] = \dfrac12(b+a),$ we have

$$
(\textrm E[X])^2 = \dfrac14(b^2+2ab+a^2).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-(\text{E}[X])^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}({b}^{2}+ab+{a}^{2})-\frac{1}{4}({b}^{2}+2ab+{a}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{4}{12}({b}^{2}+ab+{a}^{2})-\frac{3}{12}({b}^{2}+2ab+{a}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(4{b}^{2}+4ab+4{a}^{2})-\frac{1}{12}(3{b}^{2}+6ab+3{a}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{12}({b}^{2}-2ab+{a}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(b-a)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
